questions.q: What is a business event in Oracle Fusion?
options: A scheduled report that runs weekly
A system-generated notification raised at a specific lifecycle moment, like an invoice being created
A manual task a user must perform every day
A type of HTTP status code
questions.explain: Business events are system-raised notifications tied to lifecycle actions.

questions.q: Where is a business event turned on for a given Financials module?
options: It's always on by default for every module
An "Enable Business Events" profile option in Setup and Maintenance, set per module
By editing a REST request header
It cannot be turned on at all
questions.explain: Business events are enabled per module via a Setup and Maintenance profile option.

questions.q: What is the main practical difference between polling and event-driven integration?
options: Polling repeatedly asks if anything changed; event-driven is pushed the instant something happens
They are exactly the same thing
Event-driven integrations never use OIC
Polling only works with PATCH requests
questions.explain: Polling repeatedly checks; event-driven pushes notifications immediately.

questions.q: What typically subscribes to a Fusion business event in a real implementation?
options: A spreadsheet
Oracle Integration Cloud, via its ERP Cloud adapter
The Fusion database directly, with no adapter
Nothing can subscribe to a business event
questions.explain: OIC's ERP Cloud adapter is the typical subscriber to Fusion business events.

questions.q: What is a downside of a polling-based integration compared to an event-driven one?
options: Polling has no downsides
Polling introduces delay between when something happens and the next scheduled check, plus wasted calls checking for "nothing new"
Polling is always faster than event-driven integration
Polling cannot use the GET method
questions.explain: Polling adds latency and wastes calls compared to an immediate event push.
